replace.why: Real MotorInclude.h lines 72..75 are four `extern interrupt void ..._isr(void);` prototypes; `interrupt` is a C28x keyword and MSVC reports C2054. Dropping the keyword leaves plain void(void) prototypes: no function name or parameter changes, and the patch is host-only, so the target build is unaffected.

Real DSP2803x_PieVect.h line 9. MotorVF does not touch PieVectTable, but the case shim's DSP2803x_Device.h includes this header exactly as the real device header does, so it must parse. Only the keyword is removed; the struct layout is untouched.

MotorVF.c includes MotorVFInclude.h, and that header sits in include/motor/ next to the REAL SubPrgInclude.h. Left quoted, MSVC resolves it from the including file's own directory and gets the unpatched copy with the two `long int` prototypes -- the gen_dir copy is never reached and the build dies with C2632. Angle brackets drop the same-directory rule; gen_dir is first on the include path, so the patched copy wins. Same trap MotorVCInclude.h hit in the MotorVCMain case.

`extern int absl(long int);` (line 76) and `extern int qatan(long int);` (line 78). The case shim ends with `#define int short`, so `long int` expands to `long short` and MSVC rejects it (C2632). `long` and `long int` are the same type, so the width is unchanged. MotorVF calls neither, but the header has to parse because it also declares qsin / qsqrt / atan / PID / abs, which it does call.
